the deletion of the tumor-suppressor protein merlin in the neurons of the peripheral nervous systems leads to impaired functional regeneration after sciatic nerve crush-injury.
the conditional deletion of merlin in the peripheral nervous system results in an impairment of functional nerve regeneration after injury.
The tumor suppressor merin is required for proper functional recovery of peripheral nerves after injury.

the molecular mechanisms underlying peripheral nerve regeneration.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the tumor suppressor gene NF2, which is mutated in the human tumor syndrome NF2, is not only important for growth control of Schwann cells, but that it is also important for the regeneration of peripheral nerves.
the tumor suppressor protein Merlin has a dual function in the peripheral nervous system: it inhibits the growth of Schwann cells and it regulates the function of axons.
merlin is an important regulator of functional recovery after peripheral nerve injury and that the loss of this function may contribute to the pathophysiology of NF2 patients.

the tumor suppressor protein Merlin, which is mutated in the herediatary tumor disorder Neurofibromatostis type 2 (or NF2 for short) is not only a growth inhibitor for the Schwann cells of the peripheral nervous systems but it also regulates the function and regeneration of the axons themselves.
merlin is an important player in the regulation of functional nerve regeneration and that its deletion in the neuronal compartment impairs this process.
